title: ChatWeave Message (draft 0.1)
description: DRAFT. A chat message as persisted by the host and synced to clients: an ordered list of content blocks plus a mandatory plain-text fallback. After reconnect or offline, the persisted message (higher rev) always wins over a locally assembled stream state.

id.description: Message id. User messages: generated by the sending client (UUIDv7 recommended), doubling as the idempotency key for offline queues and retries; the server validates and adopts it unchanged, and the optimistic local copy is reconciled by this same id. Assistant / system messages: server-generated only.

status.description: streaming: still being produced. paused: the run is waiting for the user to answer an interrupt (see 'interrupt'); the same message resumes after the answer (docs/protocol.md 4.8). complete: finished normally. interrupted: producer stopped early (crash, cancel, upstream failure, unanswered interrupt expired); content so far is kept. error: nothing usable was produced; fallbackText explains.

fallbackText.description: Whole-message plain text. Always present, also for status 'error'. Markdown-only clients render just this.

rev.description: Persisted revision. 0 while the message has not ended (streaming or paused checkpoints); 1 when the message is first completed; +1 for every later change (e.g. a choice block resolved).

lastSeq.description: Only on checkpoints of a message that has not ended (rev 0): seq of the last event folded into this version. Required while paused. A synced checkpoint replaces local state only if lastSeq >= the locally applied seq; ended messages (rev >= 1) never carry it.

interrupt.description: Present exactly while status is 'paused': the one open interrupt the run is waiting on (docs/protocol.md 4.8). Aligned with AG-UI 1.0 Interrupt (RUN_FINISHED outcome 'interrupt').

metadata.description: Opaque host data (e.g. trace ids). Never rendered by the library.

steps.description: Compact run trace (docs/protocol.md 4.7): the steps the assistant took while producing this message, in step.started order. Stored separately from blocks: steps take no block index, are not counted in blockCount and are never part of fallbackText. Each entry holds only id, host-written label, state, duration, an optional host-written one-line summary, the block a step asked the user through (blockId), and for nested steps the enclosing delegate step (parentStepId). Never tool names, sub-agent names, arguments, raw results or model text (including reasoning). Omitted when there were no steps. Checked by the library, not expressible here: step ids are unique within the message; parentStepId names an earlier step of kind 'delegate' (so no cycles); nesting depth <= 3; at most one step is awaiting_user and it is the interrupt's step.

view.description: RESERVED for the Phase 2 View protocol (layout planning that references block data by id). Must not be emitted in 0.1; clients ignore it.

steps.$comment: Once the message has ended, every step has ended too: the producer emits step.finished for each started step before message.end.

allOf.$comment: A paused message carries exactly one open interrupt, its lastSeq, and exactly one awaiting_user step (the interrupt's step). Any other status carries no interrupt and no awaiting_user step.

Client-generated user message ids double as idempotency keys, so they must be long enough to be unique (same rule as action ids). The former separate clientMessageId field was removed (see decisions D43).
Steps belong to assistant / system messages only.

stepId.description: Stable within its message; pairs step.started with step.finished (maps to AG-UI stepName).

stepLabel.description: Host-written, user-facing description of the step, e.g. 'Checking this week's weather in Beijing'. Never a raw tool name, tool arguments or model output.

stepSummary.description: Optional host-written one-line result note from a per-tool template, e.g. 'Found 3 tasks' or 'Weather service unavailable'. Never raw results or model output.

stepEndState.description: succeeded / failed (affects only this step) / cancelled (still running or waiting when the user stopped the generation, or its interrupt expired). Waiting for the user is not an end state: the step is awaiting_user while the message is paused and returns to running when the answer arrives (docs/protocol.md 4.8).

stepKind.description: 'delegate': the step hands work to a sub-agent; the sub-agent's own steps nest under it via parentStepId (collapsed by default in the process strip). Omitted for ordinary steps (a tool call or other unit of work). The sub-agent's internal name is never sent; the host-written label describes the delegation.

interruptId.description: Opaque id of one interrupt (maps to AG-UI Interrupt.id). Unique within the message.

interrupt.description: What a paused run is waiting for. The question itself is the interaction block (blockId) in the content; the step (stepId) is the one that asked and is awaiting_user. Expiry comes from the block's action.expiresAt.

reason.description: AG-UI 1.0 core reason values: 'confirmation' (approve or decline an operation, e.g. a confirmation block before a tool runs) or 'input_required' (the agent needs an answer, e.g. a choice or form_intent block from an ask_user tool).

otherInput.description: Whether the interrupt's card offers the fixed 'other input' entry besides its own controls (docs/protocol.md 4.8, D60): the user may answer with free text instead ({freeText} on the block's action), which the host's agent interprets. Default true; a host may turn it off per interrupt (e.g. a pure confirm / cancel). Not part of AG-UI; carried in Interrupt.metadata when converting.

durationMs.description: Working time of the step in milliseconds (a duration, not a point in time). Time spent paused waiting for the user is not counted.

parentStepId.description: For a sub-agent's step: the enclosing delegate step. Absent for the main agent's top-level steps.

state.description: running: in progress (also a delegate step whose sub-agent is waiting on the user). awaiting_user: this step asked the user and the message is paused on its interrupt. Neither appears in a message that has ended.

blockId.description: The interaction block (choice / confirmation / form_intent) in this message's content through which this step asked the user. Required while awaiting_user; kept after the answer so the step row can show it.
